mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% (using 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.5%, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.5% (using 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS are below their 3-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (UNRATE < 4.5% and declining), wage pressures and anticipated Fed tightening lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5% and declining (using 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals a weakening supply chain, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 6mo_MA (using 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, supporting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is rising (using 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months signals strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST has increased for 3 consecutive months (using 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a deteriorating labor market, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 0.2pp increase in 3 months and PAYEMS < 0.5% decline in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises by >0.2pp and PAYEMS declines by >0.5% over 3 months.
